label: Explainers & diagrams
intent: Teach something. Accuracy of the labelled content matters as much as the picture.

recipes.goal: A step-by-step visual sequence, like a film's pre-production board.
recipes.when: Showing stages: how something is made, how a suit goes on, how a routine progresses.
recipes.text:
Create a single {ratio} image: a numbered process board laid out as a 4 by 2 grid of eight panels, reading left to right, top to bottom.
SUBJECT — {subject}. The same subject appears in every panel, at the same scale and the same camera distance, so the eight panels read as a single continuous sequence.
PROGRESSION — each panel advances the process by one clear step. The change between adjacent panels should be obvious at a glance and nothing else in the frame should move.
COMPOSITION — {composition} in every panel, {background} behind each.
LIGHTING — {lighting}, identical in all eight panels so no panel looks like a different shoot.
COLOUR — {grading}.
LABELS — a small number 1 to 8 in one corner of each panel. No other text anywhere.
RENDER — {render}, consistent across all panels.

image.accepts: a photo of the subject or the starting state
image.skeleton:
Use the supplied image as the reference for the subject of this process board. Keep the subject recognisably identical in all eight panels.

Create a single {ratio} image: a numbered process board as a 4 by 2 grid of eight panels read left to right, top to bottom, showing {subject} advancing one clear step per panel. Same subject, same scale, same camera distance throughout so it reads as one continuous sequence. {composition} in every panel, {background} behind each, {lighting} identical throughout, {grading}, {render}. A small number 1 to 8 in one corner of each panel; no other text.

negatives: no more than a single digit of text per panel
recipes.example: Create a single 16:9 image: a numbered process board as a 4 by 2 grid of eight panels, reading left to right, top to bottom, showing a firefighter putting on a full protective suit. PROGRESSION — boots, trousers, jacket, harness, mask, helmet, gloves, final check. One step per panel; nothing else changes. COMPOSITION — full-body in every panel, same scale and camera distance, seamless warm grey behind each. LIGHTING — even flat studio light, identical in all eight. COLOUR — neutral and true. LABELS — a small number 1 to 8 in the lower-left corner of each panel; no other text. RENDER — studio catalogue photography, consistent throughout.

recipes.goal: A poster that communicates one body of information clearly.
recipes.when: A single dense explainer: a timeline, a comparison, a set of figures you want to look designed.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} infographic poster about {subject}.
STRUCTURE — a clear top-to-bottom hierarchy: title block at the top, the main visual in the middle, supporting detail below. Everything sits on one consistent baseline grid.
MAIN VISUAL — the central diagram or chart must be genuinely informative: axes or sequence labelled, proportions visually accurate, no decorative data that means nothing.
TYPOGRAPHY — {type} throughout; set the title "{text}" as the largest element, then a clear three-level hierarchy of heading, label and caption. All text must be real, correctly spelled and readable — never placeholder glyphs.
COMPOSITION — {composition} with generous margins.
BACKGROUND — {background}.
COLOUR — {grading}, with a two-colour accent used consistently to mean the same thing everywhere.
negatives: no decorative elements that carry no information
no more than three type sizes
recipes.example: Create a 2:3 infographic poster explaining how a guitar's tone circuit works. STRUCTURE — title block at the top, a large annotated cutaway in the middle, a small parts list below, all on one baseline grid. MAIN VISUAL — the cutaway labels every component: pickups, volume pot, tone pot, capacitor and output jack, with the signal path drawn as one continuous line. TYPOGRAPHY — monospaced technical throughout; title "TONE, EXPLAINED" as the largest element, then component labels, then one-line captions. All text real and correctly spelled. COMPOSITION — symmetrical with generous margins. BACKGROUND — seamless white. COLOUR — neutral and true with one amber accent marking the signal path only.

recipes.goal: Put variants side by side so the differences are the point.
recipes.when: A/B options, before-and-after, versions of a design, competing approaches.
recipes.text:
Create a single {ratio} image: a side-by-side comparison sheet split into equal panels by thin vertical rules.
SUBJECT — {subject}. Each panel shows the same subject with exactly one variable changed. Everything else — framing, scale, lighting, background — must be identical across panels so the single difference is unmistakable.
PANELS — give each one a short {type} label at the top stating what is different about it. Labels must be real words, correctly spelled, no longer than three words.
COMPOSITION — {composition} in every panel.
BACKGROUND — {background}. LIGHTING — {lighting}. COLOUR — {grading}.
RENDER — clean designed layout, perfectly aligned panel edges, equal panel widths.
negatives: no more than three words per label
recipes.example: Create a single 16:9 comparison sheet split into three equal panels by thin vertical rules, comparing three lighting setups on the same ceramic vase. SUBJECT — the same matte ceramic vase, identical framing, scale and white background in all three panels. PANELS — labelled "HARD", "SOFT" and "RIM" in bold geometric sans at the top of each. The only difference between panels is the light. COMPOSITION — centred hero in each. BACKGROUND — seamless white. LIGHTING — hard single source, then softbox with fill, then rim light on dark. COLOUR — neutral and true. RENDER — clean designed layout, perfectly aligned edges, equal panel widths.
